memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: Gather all the plunder of the town into the middle of the public square and completely burn the town and all its plunder as a whole burnt offering to the Lord your God. That town is to remain a ruin forever, never to be rebuilt, and none of the condemned things are to be found in your hands. Then the Lord will turn from his fierce anger, will show you mercy, and have compassion on you, and will increase your numbers, as he promised on oath to your ancestors. - Deut 13:16-17 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
In this severe command about a town given over to idolatry, one striking detail stands out: none of the plunder was to be kept. Everything was to be destroyed, "none of the condemned things... found in your hands." Unlike ordinary battles where soldiers might keep spoils, here the people were to take nothing for themselves. This guarded against a subtle temptation — the temptation to profit personally from what was under God's judgment, to let greed quietly compromise their obedience.

This was a specific covenant law for Israel, and we do not carry out such judgments today. But there is an enduring principle here worth pausing on: we must not try to hold on to, or benefit from, what God has condemned. When God calls us to put something to death in our lives — a sin, a compromise, an idol — we are not to secretly keep a piece of it for ourselves. The temptation is real. We may agree to give up a sin in general while quietly clinging to some benefit it brings us.

True repentance holds nothing back. It does not negotiate with sin or keep souvenirs of what God has called us to abandon. Notice too the tender promise at the end: when the people obeyed fully, God would "show you mercy, and have compassion on you." Wholehearted obedience opens the way for God's mercy and compassion to flow. And ultimately, our confidence rests not in our perfect obedience but in Christ, who dealt with sin completely. When God calls you to let something go, let it go entirely — keep nothing back — and receive His mercy with open hands.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
- When God calls me to abandon a sin, do I secretly keep a piece of it?
- Am I tempted to hold on to some benefit from what God has condemned?
- What would wholehearted repentance, keeping nothing back, look like for me?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, when You call me to let go of sin, help me keep nothing back — no souvenirs, no secret benefits. Give me wholehearted repentance that holds nothing in reserve. Thank You for Your mercy and compassion, and for Christ who dealt with my sin completely. Amen.
